blindSummary:
This state/province replicates the festival-screening mechanism documented elsewhere in the country: in its least-developed district, Hindu-nationalist mass-organisation members objected to non-Hindu sponsors and participants at community festival events, claiming damage to "cultural purity," and pressed religion-gated entry conditions — a sectarian mark applied at the gate, a devotional recitation before start, and a deity-affiliation poster circulated to organisers — with at least three festival nights called off and tickets cancelled after written objections; police received a memorandum and arranged venue security. It is the same outing mechanism as in an adjacent large state, minus the national-ID document checks: a religion-screened gate at a public festival examines and outs gender-nonconforming visitors via actors who are not supposed to be involved. Unlike that state, no transgender welfare board has been constituted here.

Additionally, in November 2024 a transgender woman was stabbed to death and dumped in an abandoned quarry in a contract killing (~USD 14,000 equivalent) over rival claims to a community leadership seat; five suspects were arrested. It is a single incident with no sourced second instance, recorded for pattern awareness rather than as a decisive factor.

The combination of festival-entrance screening (visitor-facing, seasonal, outing mechanism) and the absence of any official welfare apparatus marks this state/province as running behind the country's board-constituted states on both protection and recognition; the exposure at festivals is community-organiser-driven at private-adjacent events.
blindSourceSummaries: A national daily's state edition (23 Sep 2025): Hindu-nationalist organisations' leaders in the state's poorest district objected to non-Hindu garba sponsors and participants as damaging "cultural purity", demanded sectarian gate marks, devotional recitation and a deity poster at venues, and warned of direct intervention; at least three festival nights were called off and tickets cancelled, a memorandum was filed with the administration, and police arranged venue deployment.

A national daily's state edition (22 Nov 2024): a transgender woman was lured out, stabbed and dumped in an abandoned quarry in a contract killing orchestrated by a rival to block her ascent to the community head seat; five suspects were arrested and most of the payment seized.

The government's official press portal, upper-house reply (8 Dec 2021, the responsible minister): 12 of the country's states/provinces and centrally administered territories had constituted transgender welfare boards under the 2020 national rules; this state/province is absent from the list.
